Decoded first-frame nonzero-alpha bounds are x33..147/y67..92; alpha≥64 bounds
are x67..112/y68..91. Thus the native up/down source-plane blur is horizontally
extended after owner Rotation90. The unchanged imported screen Direction0 would
be vertical. Uniform Scale200 converts the native pixel length control to screen
length40; this coordinate-unit conversion does **not** claim equal native/FX
sampling kernels, Gaussian tails, alpha or raster fidelity.

Executable fresh-import assertion:
`structure_document::directional_plane::tests::native_directional_blur_uses_rotated_scaled_source_plane`.
It expects one editable DirectionalBlur with Direction90/Length40 (RED before the
repair: Direction0/Length20). Supplementary native-byte Transform edits are tested
by `directional_plane_import_responds_to_native_transform_input_edits`: Scale300
→Length60, Rotation−45→Direction−45, and nonuniform/negative scale remain outside
the profile. These offline input mutations are not independent native export/edit
proof.

Import profile: ordinary unparented selected-root 2D square-pixel Solid, sole
active DirectionalBlur, static expression-free Direction/Length and uniform
positive Scale/ZRotation, no masks/matte/preserve-transparency. Other profiles
retain the existing approximation. Effect identity and owner Transform remain
editable; no image/video flattening or effect bounds/collapse change.

**Incomplete proof:** fresh FX pixels and alpha comparison, independently inspected
